sentences.text: [solemn] Every April fourteenth, India's firefighters remember the day a ship rained gold on Bombay.
In nineteen forty-four, a ship called the Fort Stikine sat in the docks with fourteen hundred tons of explosives and crates of gold.
Then cotton in the hold caught fire, and firemen pumped in so much water it started to boil.
So why didn't anyone get the explosives off?
Nobody gave the order in time, and that afternoon it blew up.
[lowering their voice] More than eight hundred people died, sixty-six of them firemen, and the blast threw gold bars across the city.
Workers were still pulling those bars out of the harbour mud in two thousand eleven, and every one went back to the government.
[matter-of-fact] I think whoever found one should have been allowed to keep it.
